title: A braking force is not a constant coordinate deceleration
promptMarkdown: A particle of invariant mass $m$ moves initially at $3c/5$ along $+x$ in laboratory $S$. A constant force $f_x=-F$ ($F>0$) acts until it first stops. Find its laboratory stopping time and stopping distance, the elapsed proper time, and the magnitude of proper acceleration. Check the work–energy relation and compare with the low-speed formula using a general initial speed $v_0\ll c$.
hintLadder: Solve $dp/dt=-F$ before trying to solve for $v(t)$.
The chain rule cancels the factor $\cosh\theta$ in $dp/dt$ when $dt/d\tau=\cosh\theta$.
